body:
Routed from the getwyrd/wyrd-pdca Act review of 2026-08-02. Follow-up to **#324** (the backstop) and **#359** (the calibration loop); the enabling mechanism is **#371**.

## The observation

`size_signal`'s strongest rule is *rounds already spent ≥ 2* — 76% precision that a third round follows, and the one rule with no size component. It counts **rounds**, without asking what a round was spent on.

Bundle `issue_652` (getwyrd/wyrd-pdca) fired the backstop on that rule alone:

```json
{ "patch_bytes": 66243, "patch_files": 4, "rounds": 3, "replans": 1, "auto_iters": 4 }
```

66 KB and 4 files — comfortably inside both the calibrated thresholds *and* that instance's own hand-set slice budget (≤1,500 semantic lines / 15 files). The §6 item nonetheless read *"this slice is behaving oversized… recommend answering `iterate-plan` and authoring the split in the re-plan"*.

At least one of those rounds was not the slice: the gating C4-ci row was red because the **host's `cargo-deny` was too old for the gate's invocation** (filed as #435) — a cause present in neither the patch nor the brief. The sibling bundle `issue_651` demonstrably lost a Do iteration to the same environment fault.

So the recommendation on 652 was "split this slice" when the evidence was "this host had a stale CLI". The human overrode it correctly both times, but a signal that spends human attention arguing with it is the signal that gets ignored later.

## Why this is a measurement bug, not a threshold one

#359 is the right home for *"is 2 still the right number a hundred bundles later"*. This is different: the counter is measuring something other than what the rule is calibrated on. The corpus behind the 76% figure contains the same contamination — every round any bundle lost to a shimmed `cc`, an absent CLI, a read-only advisory DB, a sandbox that cannot bind loopback, or an OOM-killed leaf is in there as churn evidence. That makes the thresholds derived from it optimistic in an unknown direction, and retuning against the same corpus cannot fix it.

It is the sibling of the corpus defect #359 already records: *"`size-calibrate` cannot attribute pre-replan churn… 12 of 83 bundles"*.

## Why it is now fixable

**#371** landed the confirm-once mechanism: a gating row that fails is re-run once and a `fail→pass` is recorded flagged `flaky` with its own §6 item. The harness therefore already has a first-class marker for "this red was not the patch". Alongside it, a row recorded `unverifiable` is by construction not a verdict on the patch either.

## Ask

1. `size_signal` should count **rounds attributable to the slice** — exclude a round whose gating failure was recorded `flaky` (#371) or `unverifiable`.
2. Whatever attribution lands should also be applied by `scripts/size-calibrate` when mining the corpus, so the precision figures are re-derived on attributed rounds. Report whether the numbers move (as #359 asks for the `iteration-v*/brief.md` question).
3. If full attribution is too coarse to infer for historical bundles, the fallback is honesty in the item rather than silence: have the §6 text name the rule that fired and the round count it used, so a human can see at a glance that a 66 KB / 4-file slice was flagged purely on rounds.

## Deliberately not proposed

Raising the threshold. The rule is right; the input is contaminated. A retune would trade recall for a defect that would still be there.

## Origin

getwyrd/wyrd-pdca Act review 2026-08-02 (`process/act-log.md`), bundles issue_651 / issue_652 — two firings, two human overrides, one of them traceable to #435.
title: size-signal counts rounds lost to environment faults as churn — the backstop recommends splitting a slice for a stale host CLI
